spec.name: labour
spec.rationale: Payrolls alone. The single fastest read; no cross-confirmation.

series.label: Nonfarm payrolls
series.note: The fastest broad read on the economy, and the one the rest wait for.

series.label: Industrial production
series.note: Cyclical and volatile; turns before the labour market.

series.label: Real retail sales
series.note: Consumption in volume terms, so inflation does not leak into growth.

series.label: Real consumption
series.note: Two thirds of output, but it publishes three weeks behind payrolls.

series.label: Real disposable income
series.note: What funds the consumption above; turns earlier in an income shock.

series.label: CPI
series.note: Headline. What households and index-linked contracts actually face.

series.label: Core CPI
series.note: Ex food and energy; less noisy, and slower to turn.

series.label: Producer prices
series.note: Upstream, so it leads consumer prices when the shock is a cost shock.

fast.name: fast
fast.rationale: Two of the quickest broad series. Least lag, narrowest evidence.

broad.name: broad
broad.rationale: Five growth series and three price series. Most evidence, dragged to the slowest member's publication date.

core.name: core
core.rationale: Core inflation instead of headline: fewer energy head-fakes, slower to register a real one.

production.name: production

fast_1m.name: fast_1m
fast_1m.rationale: One month of rate-of-change. Maximum responsiveness, maximum noise.

fast_6m.name: fast_6m
fast_6m.rationale: Six months. Smooth enough to miss a turn until it is obvious.

broad_6m.name: broad_6m
broad_6m.rationale: Broad evidence on a slow clock — the most conservative reading here.

selection.criterion: among specifications whose median spell clears the persistence floor of 2 months, the highest share of real-time labels that survived revision, measured on the training window; ties to the shorter publication lag

disqualified.fast_1m: median spell 1.0 months is below the 2-month floor — this labels months, not regimes
